messages:
maria: Heads-up — since ~02:10 UTC we're seeing periodic tail-latency spikes on inference pods in ap-northeast1-rackB. Noticed on dashboards: token p95 jumps and some requests time out.

maria: Quick correlation: GPU telemetry shows recoverable ECC counter jumps and VRM temps oscillating quickly (85C -> 95C -> 82C) on a subset of cards in node gpu-node-45. That pattern aligns with clock throttles.

ben: Can you paste the perif telemetry + nvidia-smi snippet? also check kern log for Xid and PCI errors.

maria: pasted output: 
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,temperature.memory,clocks.gr,utilization.gpu,power.draw,psu.temp --format=csv,noheader
0, A100-80GB, 88, 84, 598, 92 %, 285.2 W, 49
1, A100-80GB, 93, 86, 350, 12 %, 210.7 W, 48
2, A100-80GB, 86, 83, 594, 95 %, 287.8 W, 50
```
and kernel excerpt: 
```
Apr 12 02:12:07 gpu-node-45 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=1234, chid=5, reason: MMU fault
Apr 12 02:12:07 gpu-node-45 kernel: nvidia: GPU 1: recoverable ECC error count increased
Apr 12 02:12:09 gpu-node-45 kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00: RAS reported link error, power transition?
```

maria: Also saw power-sensor dips on BMC telemetry at same times (rail_vgpu dropping ~5-8W briefly).

carol: That sounds like VRM thermal hysteresis triggering frequency down/up loops. If VRM thermistor is noisy you get repeated throttles. We saw similar with bad thermal paste contact.

dan: Agree. Could be localized heatsink mounting or a flaky VRM temp sensor. Quick triage: move inference pods off that node and put it into maintenance so we can run a hardware check.

maria: I'm going to drain it now. command: `kubectl drain gpu-node-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120`

infra-bot: Alert: node gpu-node-45 cordoned by maria at 2026-04-12T02:18:40Z — draining pods (infra-bot id 9021).

ben: Before you evict everything, consider setting a temporary reduced power-limit on the suspect GPUs to avoid repeated clocks changes: `nvidia-smi -i 1 -pl 230` (set to safe lower bound) — that can keep clocks stable so workloads continue while we stage repairs. Note: will affect throughput/cost.

maria: Did a graceful drain and moved ~18 inference pods to rackA spares. Observed immediate drop in tail-latency spikes after migration.

carol: Good. Next steps for hardware: request onsite tech to reseat heatsink and reflow thermal interface, inspect VRM thermistor traces. If hardware swap not possible immediately, plan to RMA card.

dan: Also schedule a short BIOS/firmware update window for that node's server — older BMC firmware showed weird PSU mux behavior in the past. Put it in next maintenance slot (tonight 22:00 UTC).

ben: Long-term: add an alert that fires on pattern: (recoverable_ecc_delta > 10 within 5m) AND (gpu_temp_vrm oscillation > 6C within 2m) AND (power_draw_delta > 5W short dips). Current alerts are too coarse. Will file follow-up.

maria: Logged a JIRA ticket: INFRA-8459 with attached logs and pointer to node. Assigned to paul for hardware triage.

paul: I'll pick this up. Onsite tech ETA 03:30 UTC. I'll run memtest, re-seat heatsink, and capture high-sample telemetry. Also will check PSU rail readings on the PDUs for simultaneous dips.

maria: Thanks. For the record: temporary mitigation steps we used: 1) drain node, 2) migrate pods to spares, 3) temporary power-limit on suspect GPU, 4) open hardware ticket + schedule BIOS window.

carol: FYI — we're slightly overprovisioned this week so moving these pods cost is covered; if this becomes frequent we'll need to budget spare-capacity differently.

ben: I'll implement the composite alert and a quick automated runbook that can cordon + nudge power-limit before manual intervention.

maria: Closing out here once paul confirms repair. Will post follow-up status in INFRA-8459 and drop a short postmortem if RMA happens. :white_check_mark:
